turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, Mrs Keane. Take a seat there. How have you been keeping?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Grand.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She's not grand, doctor, not really. The ankles are up again and she's breathless on the stairs.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right so, swollen ankles and shortness of breath. How long has that been with her?
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Two weeks. Well, actually, nearer three weeks. It came on after we were down in Tralee.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Three.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Three weeks. Any chest pain along with the breathlessness?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And a cough, especially lying down at night?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0011] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She is wrecked tired though. Asleep in the chair half the afternoon. The swelling gets worse if she sits too long.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ok. I'll get the numbers while I'm thinking. Blood pressure is one-sixty-four over ninety. No, scratch that, I misread it. One-fifty-eight over ninety-two.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is seventy-eight. Oxygen is ninety-six percent. Temperature is thirty-six point four degrees.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both ankles are pitting, the swelling up as far as the shins. Lungs are clear, I don't hear any crackles. Heart sounds are regular.
[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I live in with her and I do the pill box, so I know what's going in.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grand, walk me through the box.

[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): In the morning there's the water tablet, then the little white one for the heart, and the heart tablet, the bisoprolol, as well. A yellow one at night for the cholesterol. And she had another blood pressure tablet, but your man in the hospital stopped that one.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me think this out. The little white one and the bisoprolol — are those two tablets, or the one tablet written down twice?
[SEG0019] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's the same one. Little white tablet with a line down the middle. I had it on the list twice. My mistake.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): So we're not double-dosing. Bisoprolol two and a half milligrams, once in the morning?
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yes.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the water tablet is the furosemide. What strength is printed on the box?
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Twenty milligrams. No, wait, I always say that wrong. It's forty. Forty milligrams, one every morning.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Forty milligrams of furosemide each morning, grand. And the yellow cholesterol one?
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Atorvastatin, twenty milligrams at night. The high blood pressure itself, she's had that five-ish years.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the tablet the hospital doctor stopped — the name and the dose, if you have them?
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Amlodipine, five milligrams. Stopped about six weeks ago. He said the ankles were from it. They're back all the same.

[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Amlodipine is stopped. She's still on the bisoprolol, the furosemide forty, and the atorvastatin twenty. Thinking it through, the fluid is back even without the amlodipine, so forty of the water tablet isn't holding her.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok.

[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll change the furosemide. I was going to make it eighty milligrams in one go — no, that's too much of a jump with that blood pressure. Keep the forty in the morning and add twenty milligrams at lunchtime.
[SEG0031] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll put the extra one in the lunch slot of the box.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please do. Ignore the eighty, that was me thinking aloud. Forty in the morning, twenty at lunch, and nothing else new.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Because we're changing the water tablet I want a kidney blood test, the U and E. I was going to send you down now, but the phlebotomy clinic is finished for the day. We'll book it for tomorrow morning.
[SEG0034] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can bring her in the morning, no bother.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep the legs up when she's in the chair, and go easy on the salt. Don't be shaking it over the dinner.
[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She does love her rashers.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): A rasher now and again is grand. Just mind the salt cellar.

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): My impression, and it's only a working one, is that fluid is building up again — a small bit of heart failure, not the amlodipine, since that's been off about six weeks. The blood test will show if the kidneys mind the extra water tablet.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Home?
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Home, yes. Come back and see me in two weeks. If the breathing gets worse or the swelling shoots up before that, ring and we'll see her sooner.
[SEG0041] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will. Thanks, doctor.
